claims.text: Materials with a high density of states at the Fermi level can exhibit superconductivity at low temperatures.
Certain crystal structures can provide a high density of states at the Fermi level.
Cooling the proposed material to low temperature can induce a transition from a normal conducting state to a superconducting state.
Crystal structure is the structural mediator of the proposed superconducting behavior.
Density functional theory predicts that materials with a high density of states at the Fermi level can exhibit superconductivity.
A high density of states at the Fermi level increases electron-phonon interactions.
Increased electron-phonon interactions cause the proposed superconducting behavior.
The predicted superconducting state has zero electrical resistance.
The predicted superconducting state exhibits perfect diamagnetism.
The material is in a normal conducting state at high temperatures.
Superconductivity is expected only below the material's critical temperature.
The exact critical temperature and superconducting properties cannot be predicted reliably without specifying the material composition and crystal structure.
